10.8.text: Because an assignment through an back_inserter iterator calls the push_back operation. (p.382) That is, the insertion (or resizing) is handled by the container's operation and not the algorithm.

10.10.name: 10.10.md
10.10.text: Because algorithms operate on a FIXED range of iterators. Changing the size of a container would invalidate the iterators, in which case the algorithm would have to refresh the iterators. This duplicates work and makes the algorithm functions do more than what their name suggests or should. It is a better design to leave the container related tasks (such as resizing) to the container's operations.

10.26.name: 10.26.md
10.26.text: back_inserter, front_inserter and inserter are analogous to c.push_pack, push_front and c.insert container operations. In fact, whenever we create one of these insert iterators, it calls its corresponding container operation to handle the insertion into a container. Therefore, the way these iterators insert and refresh the iterator in the elements range resembles the operation each iterator uses.

10.38.name: 10.38.md
10.38.text:
From Table 10.5 (p.410)

1) Input iterator

```text
Read, but not write, single-pass, increment only
```

2) Output iterator

```text
Write, but not read, singe-pass, increment only
```

3) Forward iterator

```text
Read, write, multi-pass, increment only
```

4) Bidirectional iterator

```text
Read, write, multi-pass, increment and decrement
```

5) Random-access iterator

```text
Read, write, multi-pass, full iterator arithmetic
```

10.39.name: 10.39.md
10.39.text: A list has a bidirectional iterator, while a vector has a random-access iterator.

10.40.name: 10.40.md
10.40.text:
The copy function requires a minimum input iterators for its first two arguments and an output for its third (the destination iterator).

The reverse function requires a minimum a bidirectional iterators, because the algorithm requires read, write, and multi-pass access, and bidirectional movement through the container.

The unique function requires a minimum forward iterators, because the algorithm requires read, write and multi-pass access, but not bidirectional movement through the container.
